Each node is shaded by how many maximal cliques contain it: C sits in both, so it has 2 and the darkest shading, while A, B and D have 1 each, as the table lists." width="100%"} For every node, how many maximal cliques it belongs to. Nodes in many cliques bridge several tightly knit groups (people in several close circles, proteins in several complexes), which makes this a simple overlap and brokerage indicator. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of nodes (IDs or labels) to report. If `None` (default), all nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID to the number of maximal cliques containing it. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Counts memberships in the maximal cliques of `find_cliques()`, as NetworkX's `number_of_cliques` does. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~node_clique_number`) : The size of the largest clique at each node. [](`~find_cliques`) : List all maximal cliques. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `C` is in two maximal cliques, the triangle and the edge `C`-`D`. The others are in one each: ::: {#15ebd870 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")] ) graph.set_node_attrs("cliques", graph.number_of_cliques()) graph.get_node_df().select("label", "cliques") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Members of many circles `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. The administrator `33` is in 14 of its 36 maximal cliques, and the instructor `0` in 13. Each belongs to many small groups rather than one large one, while 12 members are in just one clique: ::: {#a5579842 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() karate.set_node_attrs("cliques", karate.number_of_cliques()) ( karate.get_node_df() .sort("cliques", descending=True) .select("label", "role", "degree", "cliques") .head(5) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
